commit_message:
[Metal] Support external executables in the MetalSPIRV target

The CUDA, ROCm and Vulkan targets serialize external variants (those with no
inner module, from hal.executable.source or hal.dispatch.extern) from their
objects; the MetalSPIRV target dereferenced the missing inner module.

An external Metal variant has exactly one object: a precompiled .metallib,
recognized by its "MTLB" magic, or MSL source, which is compiled to a
metallib like generated MSL (or embedded as source with
--iree-metal-compile-to-metallib=false). Each export names a kernel in the
object and must have a workgroup_size, used as the threadgroup size.
Kernels follow the generated code's ABI: bindings in an argument buffer at
[[buffer(0)]], constants as 32-bit values at [[buffer(3)]].

Generated and external variants now share the FlatBuffer packing, which
places each PipelineDef and its debug info at the export's ordinal, as the
runtime looks pipelines up by ordinal and createExportDefs indexes debug
info by it; missing, out-of-range and duplicate ordinals are errors, as in
the CUDA target. Pipelines were previously in declaration order. The
default pipeline renumbers ordinals in declaration order before
serialization, so this only showed when serializing a hal.executable
directly.

Adds a lit test for both object kinds, out-of-order ordinals and the error
cases, and a samples/custom_dispatch/metal sample like the CUDA and Vulkan
ones, which mixes the hand-authored kernels with generated code. Both of its
examples (.metallib and MSL source) pass on an M2 Pro.

commit_message:
Keep padding from shrinking inputs that the padded op only partly reads

Padding an operation to tile-aligned sizes sizes each input to the region the
padded loops read. A strided or dilated window can leave trailing elements of an
input unread, so that region can be smaller than the input. The padding then
needed a negative amount, which tensor.pad rejects, and compilation failed, for
example for grouped convolutions on gfx942. Such inputs are now cropped to the
region that is read before they are padded, wherever IREE pads operations
through the TilingInterface.

Padding an operation to tile-aligned sizes sizes each input to the region the
padded loops read. A strided or dilated window can leave trailing elements of an
input unread, so that region can be smaller than the input. The padding then
needed a negative amount, which tensor.pad rejects, and compilation failed, for
example for grouped convolutions on gfx942. Such inputs are now cropped to the
region that is read before they are padded, wherever IREE pads operations
through the TilingInterface.

Signed-off-by: Jelle Schuhmacher <schuehmacher@roofline.ai>

Assisted-by: Claude Code
